title: Per-tenant warm priming and SDK toggle lab
content:
Notes to self — experiment goals:

1) Reduce first-call latency variance for low-traffic tenants (<= 5 qps peak) without reserving Dedicated capacity.
2) Provide a safe SDK-level pin/toggle that product teams can use to pin a model version per-tenant and optionally request a short priming run.
3) Measure cost/benefit tradeoffs: priming tokens vs. percent slowdown avoided by cold KV-cache misses.

Background / motivation:
- We get a lot of variance from tenant cold-starts: KV cache miss + kernel path selection + JIT overhead (on some backends). For small tenants, Dedicated reserved GPU doesn't make sense.
- A small, targeted priming run (a handful of representative calls seeded after pinning) may material reduce p95s for first N calls.
- Product teams want a lightweight API/SDK primitive to opt-in per-tenant, with guardrails and telemetry baked in.

Proposed primitives (SDK-level):
- setModelPin(tenantId, model, version, opts): pin tenant -> model:version. opts: {autoPrime: boolean, primeProfile: string, ttlMinutes: int}  // default ttl 24h
- clearModelPin(tenantId)
- schedulePrime(tenantId, profileName, concurrencyHint)
- getPinStatus(tenantId) => {pinnedModel, pinnedAt, ttlRemaining, lastPrime}

Priming profile examples (small -> large):
- quick_ping: 3 requests, short prompt template, low token count (~50 tokens each)
- convo_seeder: 10 requests, multi-turn prompt (simulate 3-turn), ~400 tokens total
- embedding_warm: 8 calls to embedding endpoint with representative vectors (for embeddings-backed feature search)

Priming mechanics (server-side expectations):
- Priming should run on the same runtime pool variant the tenant will use (quantization/instance type). If not available, run on closest compatible fallback and mark as "partial primed".
- Priming requests must be flagged so they do not count towards customer metrics or influence quality evals. Tag as internal: priming=true.
- Respect concurrencyHint but cap to 2 concurrent priming workers per host to avoid eviction storms.

Telemetry / signals to capture:
- pre-prime: baseline p50/p95 latency (first 100 calls after cold restart), error rate, mean token count, tail KV-cache miss ratio if available
- post-prime: same metrics for 1h, 24h, 7d after priming; compute delta in p95 and small-sample cost delta
- priming cost: tokens used + GPU-seconds charged for priming run (separate billed bucket)
- warm fraction: % of incoming requests that hit primed state vs cold state
- priming success marker: lastPrimeSucceeded boolean, stacktrace if failed

Ramp / canary plan for SDK toggle rollout (internal staging -> prod):
- stage 0 (dev): library-level unit tests + local emulation. test sanity: setModelPin + schedulePrime triggers priming job and updates status.
- stage 1 (internal): enable for internal tenants (product and infra) only; run for 2 weeks; collect telemetry; iterate on primeProfiles.
- stage 2 (alpha): open to 5 external customers by invite; pilot churn: 2 weeks; expose UI in Console as "Tenant priming" toggle (default off).
- stage 3 (beta): SDK default off, enable flag in Console for all customers; add quota flag to prevent abuse (max 3 primes per tenant per 24h).
- stage 4 (GA): exposed in public SDK; docs, best-practice guidance; billing: priming tokens billed as-is but flagged in usage CSV.

Safety + rollback rules:
- If any priming job causes host OOM or >10% additional error rate in host pool, abort all priming in that pool and revert new priming concurrency. Notify SRE.
- Telemetry-based rollback: if p95 worsens by >10% for >=3 tenants after priming, auto-disable autoPrime for those tenants and create a ticket.
- Manual revert: clearModelPin(tenantId) will not retroactively delete primed caches, but will stop future scheduled primes and remove pinning routing. We should consider a 'evictPrimeCache(tenantId)' API for immediate rollback (needs infra support).

Operational runbook snippets (to paste into oncall doc):
- Quick check: tenant X complaining about slow first-turn responses
  * run: rwctl tenant-metrics --tenant X --lookback 1h --metrics latency_p95,errors,primed
  * if primed=false and tenant is small, recommend setModelPin(tenantX, rdm-13b, v3, {autoPrime:true}) or schedulePrime manually

- For incident: heavy priming causing host pressure
  * run: rwctl priming-jobs --list --pool <pool-id> --status RUNNING
  * cancel: rwctl priming-jobs --cancel <job-id> (or cancel all in pool)
  * escalate: @sre on-call; include priming job ids and host ids in incident ticket

Sample curl (example priming request flagging) — copyable:
curl -X POST https://api.redwood.com/v1/requests \n  -H "Authorization: Bearer $REDWOOD_API_KEY" \n  -H "Content-Type: application/json" \n  -d '{"model":"rdm-7b", "input":"seed: hello\n", "metadata": {"x-priming": true, "tenant_id":"tenant-123"}}'

SDK snippet (JS pseudo):
// high-level helper for product teams
async function pinAndPrime(tenantId, modelRef) {
  await rwClient.setModelPin(tenantId, modelRef, {autoPrime:true, primeProfile: 'quick_ping', ttlMinutes: 1440});
  // return status and link to priming job for product dashboard
  return await rwClient.getPinStatus(tenantId);
}

Open questions (things to decide before alpha):
- TTL semantics: do we count TTL as soft hint (best-effort)-or guarantee-level? If soft, customers may assume warm state longer than reality.
- Billing: do we surface priming tokens as a separate line item or include in normal usage buckets? (pref: separate flagged bucket to make cost visible)
- UI: should we surface "estimated priming cost" before users click prime? (yes)
- Cache eviction: should evictPrimeCache force a warm eviction and reset kernel cache? infra implications.

TODO (me):
- [ ] RFC draft for infra: priming job scheduler + cost tagging (due 2025-03-09)
- [ ] Prototype SDK change and unit tests (PR branch: feature/tenant-priming)
- [ ] Add metrics dashboards: priming-cost, priming-success-rate, primed-p95-delta
- [ ] Coordinate with Console team for toggle UI/confirm flows
- [ ] Write short internal playbook for SRE covering priming failures

Random ideas to keep in pocket:
- Offer "simulate prime" mode that runs priming locally in console with synthetic load estimation.
- For very latency-sensitive tenants, offer ephemeral pinned shards (short-lived dedicated workers) for an additional fee.
- Provide recommended primeProfile per model family (e.g., rdm-7b: quick_ping, rdm-13b: convo_seeder)

End of note. This is my working scratchpad — lots of rough edges. Revisit after infra RFC and one pilot run.
